EUI was used to evaluate overall building energy performance (i.e., fuel oil for heat and electricity) and The Tribal Office showed a substantial reduction of approximately 26% compared to the baseline established in 2016 (Figure 5). The observed saving could translate into financial benefits for the community, enabling the possibility of further reinvestment into infrastructure. The marked decrease, especially in winter, underscores the effectiveness of the implemented retrofits in this heating-dominated setting. LED substitution, boiler and hydronic distribution system improvements, and the installation and explanation of programmable thermostats each contributed to the overall reduction in energy use. Over the monitoring period, electricity consumption declined from 15,259 kWh to 11,262 kWh, while fuel oil consumption dropped from 850 gallons to 627 gallons. These reductions translate into meaningful financial benefits, though the precise dollar value is difficult to calculate. Reported ECIs have been adjusted to 2024-dollar values to account for inflation (Figure 5); however, such adjustments remain imperfect because of the complex financial landscape and the eight-year gap between the baseline (2016) and follow-up (2024) periods.
